81-004.r: Congress ministries resigned in 1939 (after 28 months in office) → British declared India a party to the war without Indians' consent; not cabinet failure, left-wing rise or riots.

81-005.r: Second World War: began September 1, 1939 (Germany invaded Poland); ended after six years in 1945.

81-006.r: British Prime Minister during the Second World War → Winston Churchill (tenures 1940-45 and 1951-55).

82-001.r: Word 'Pakistan' (first 'PAKSTAN') first used by Chaudhary Rahmat Ali, a Cambridge University student, in his pamphlet 'Now or Never; Are we to Live or Perish for Ever?'

82-002.r: 'Pakistan' coined by Chaudhary Rahmat Ali in a 1933 pamphlet; name formed from Punjab, Afghan Province (NWFP), Kashmir, Sindh and Balochistan.
82-002.h: P-A-K-S-tan = Punjab, Afghania, Kashmir, Sindh, BalochisTAN.

82-003.r: Idea of a separate Muslim nation → poet Muhammad Iqbal, Allahabad session of Muslim League (1930): Punjab, NWFP, Sindh, Balochistan as a single state.
82-003.t: Don't confuse: Iqbal gave the idea; Rahmat Ali coined the word 'Pakistan'; Jinnah led the demand.

82-004.r: First proposal for a separate Muslim state → Mohammad Iqbal, presidential address, Muslim League Allahabad session 1930; called Hindus and Muslims two separate nations.

82-005.r: Movement for Pakistan led by M.A. Jinnah; Muslim League Lahore session (March 22-24, 1940) under his presidency demanded a separate Muslim state.

82-006.r: Sarojini Naidu called Mohammad Ali Jinnah the 'Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity'.
82-006.h: Nightingale of India praised Jinnah's early nationalism.

82-007.r: 'Nehru is a patriot, while Jinnah is a politician' → said by Muhammad Iqbal to Nehru; recorded in Nehru's 'Discovery of India' (page 352).

82-008.r: Jinnah: supported two-nation theory; presided Muslim League Lahore session (22-24 March 1940); did not join the Non-Cooperation Movement. Untrue option: 'always had dairy'.
82-008.c: Option (d) 'He always had dairy' is garbled (probably 'diary'); explanation does not discuss it.

82-009.r: Separate Muslim homeland first got definite expression in Iqbal's presidential speech, Allahabad session of Muslim League (1930); pamphlet 'Now or Never' → Rahmat Ali.

82-011.r: Pakistan (Lahore) Resolution passed by Muslim League on March 23, 1940 at Lahore: contiguous Muslim-majority units to be grouped into separate regions.

82-013.r: Lahore Resolution (22-24 March 1940): presented by Fazal ul Haq, approved (seconded) by Khaliquzzaman; outline prepared with Sikander Hayat Khan. Among options → Khaliquzzaman.
82-013.c: Explanation says Fazal ul Haq presented (moved) it and Khaliquzzaman only approved it; answer fits only because Fazlul Haq is not an option.

82-014.r: Pakistan Resolution (Lahore, March 1940): drafted by Sikandar Hayat Khan; presented on 23 March 1940 by Fazlul Haq.

82-015.r: Jinnah's Two-Nation Theory got effect (division proposal) at Muslim League's Lahore session, 22-24 March 1940.

82-017.r: Muslim League celebrated 'Pakistan Day' on 23rd March 1943 (first observed March 23, 1941), marking the Lahore session of 1940 chaired by Jinnah.

82-019.r: 'Divide and Quit' → M.A. Jinnah (Muslim League) during the Second World War: British should first divide India into Hindustan and Pakistan, then leave.
82-019.t: Don't confuse with Gandhi's 'Quit India' slogan.

83-001.r: Individual Satyagraha (after rejecting August Proposal), 17 October 1940: first Satyagrahi Vinoba Bhave, second Jawaharlal Nehru, third Brahmdutt.
83-001.h: V-N-B order: Vinoba, Nehru, Brahma Dutt.

83-002.r: Individual Satyagraha 1940 (Gandhi): first Vinoba Bhave (started individual civil disobedience), second Jawaharlal Nehru, third Brahma Dutt.

83-006.r: Vinoba Bhave, first Satyagrahi (1940), started Individual Satyagraha from Pavnar, Maharashtra.

83-007.r: 'Sarvodaya' (Universal Uplift) first used by Mahatma Gandhi as title of his 1908 translation of Ruskin's 'Unto This Last'.

83-008.r: 17 October 1940: after rejecting August Offer, Gandhi called limited (Individual) Satyagraha by selected individuals; kept limited so as not to disrupt Britain's war effort.
83-008.c: Reason prints 'to embrace Britain's war efforts'; explanation means not to disrupt (embarrass) them, likely a misprint.

84-001.r: Cripps Mission → Stafford Cripps arrived March 1942; pressure from USA, China, Australia amid rising power of Japan.

84-002.r: Cripps proposals (March 1942): Dominion Status after war; Indian Union of provinces and states; any unit may stay outside; Indians elect constitution-making body. Not: equal-representation executive council.

84-006.r: Cripps proposal → 'post-dated cheque on a crashing (failing) bank' → Mahatma Gandhi.

84-007.r: Cripps proposals: Constitution-making body (yes); full independence (no), only Dominion Status after Second World War.

84-008.r: Cripps Mission (March 1942) sent by British PM Winston Churchill to win India's participation in Second World War.

84-009.r: Official Congress negotiators with Cripps Mission → Jawaharlal Nehru and Maulana Azad.

84-010.r: Gandhi's movements called 'Political Blackmail' → Lord Linlithgow, longest-serving Viceroy (1936-1943); Quit India launched in his tenure.

85-001.r: 6 July 1942 Congress Working Committee at Wardha, where Gandhi first discussed 'Quit India', was presided by Congress President Maulana Abul Kalam Azad.

85-002.r: Congress Working Committee passed the 'Quit India' resolution at Wardha on 14th July 1942.
85-002.t: Don't confuse: Wardha = Working Committee resolution; Bombay (Gowalia Tank) = AICC adoption in August.

85-003.r: Commander-in-Chief of Indian Army during Quit India → Lord Wavell; later Viceroy and Governor-General 1943-1947.

85-004.r: AICC session 7-8 August 1942, Gowalia Tank Maidan (now August Kranti Ground), Bombay; Quit India Movement began 9th August 1942.

85-007.r: 8th August 1942 → Quit India Resolution adopted by AICC at Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay; 1942 is known for Quit India.

85-014.r: Eve of Quit India: Gandhi asked Princes to accept their people's sovereignty; govt servants not to resign but declare allegiance to Congress; soldiers not to fire on countrymen.

85-015.r: 'We shall either free India or die in the attempt' / 'Do or Die' → Mahatma Gandhi, Quit India Movement (8 August 1942).

85-022.r: Quit India Movement launched in response to failure of Cripps Proposals (1942).

85-023.r: Baldev Sahai resigned as Advocate General in 1942, protesting arrests of leaders (Operation Zero Hour) during Quit India Movement.

85-024.r: Quit India 1942 was not purely non-violent: in first week 250 railway stations damaged, 500+ post offices and 150 police stations attacked; Gandhi refused to condemn violence.
85-024.c: Book prints no answer; explanation points to (a) 'non-violent' as the untrue statement.

85-025.r: Quit India Movement (August 1942) led by Mahatma Gandhi; next day Gandhi, Nehru and other Congress leaders arrested.

85-026.r: Quit India 1942: became spontaneous after top leaders' arrest; Gandhi, in jail, never led it; much violence; Congress declared illegal.
85-026.c: No answer printed; explanation says (a) and (c) are untrue, yet notes UPPSC accepted (b), which it calls true.

85-027.r: Did not support Quit India → Hindu Mahasabha, Communist Party of India, Unionist Party (Punjab) and Muslim League.
85-027.h: H-C-U-M stayed away: Hindu Mahasabha, Communists, Unionists, Muslim League.

85-028.r: Quit India Resolution (AICC, Bombay, August 8, 1942) moved by Jawaharlal Nehru, supported by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

85-030.r: Draft of 'Quit India' resolution prepared by Mahatma Gandhi with help of Jawaharlal Nehru and Maulana Abul Kalam Azad.

85-031.r: Slogan 'Quit India' coined by Yusuf Meher Ali.
85-031.t: Don't confuse: 'Quit India' slogan → Yusuf Meher Ali; 'Do or Die' → Gandhi.

85-032.r: Congress President when 'Quit India' resolution passed → Maulana Abul Kalam Azad (President since Ramgarh session 1940; no session held 1941-1945).

85-033.r: INC President for six consecutive years → Abul Kalam Azad.

85-034.r: 'Bihar Kesari' → Shri Krishna Singh; active in Quit India Movement (1942); first Chief Minister of Bihar after independence.

85-035.r: Quit India was a reaction to: disappointment with Cripps Mission, threat of Japanese attack, AICC's August 1942 resolution. Not: Gandhi's articles provoking violence.

85-036.r: Secret Congress Radio during Quit India → run by Usha Mehta; Ram Manohar Lohia broadcast regularly; heard up to Madras.
85-036.h: Usha = dawn; her secret radio woke the nation.

85-040.r: All India Azad Dasta → Jayaprakash Narayan, at Bakri Ka Tapu (Terai, Nepal), for guerrilla war against British during Quit India.

85-041.r: British Prime Minister during Quit India Movement → Winston Churchill (1940-1945).

85-042.r: Louis Fischer → American journalist, Gandhi's biographer, was with Gandhi during Quit India; with Pearl Buck and others he demanded India's freedom.

85-046.r: Quit India riots spread widest in Bihar and United Provinces: Azamgarh, Ballia, Gorakhpur (east UP); Gaya, Bhagalpur, Saran, Champaran, Muzaffarpur (Bihar).

85-047.r: Linlithgow called August Movement 1942 'most serious rebellion since Sepoy Mutiny' (1857) → because of massive peasant upsurge; A and R true, R explains A.

85-048.r: Arrests of August 9, 1942: Rajendra Prasad → Bankipur Jail; Gandhi and Sarojini Naidu → Aga Khan Palace, Pune; other Working Committee members (Nehru, Azad, Pant) → Ahmednagar Fort.

85-049.r: Yogendra Shukla escaped Hazaribagh jail with Jaya Prakash Narayan (November 9, 1942); re-arrested at Muzaffarpur and brought to Patna (7 December 1942).

85-050.r: Rampyari Devi, wife of Jagat Narayan Lal → addressed assembly at Bankipur during Quit India, calling people to quit government jobs.

85-051.r: After Quit India Resolution (August 1942), Gandhi was arrested in Bombay and kept with Sarojini Naidu in Aga Khan Palace, Pune.

85-053.r: After leaders' arrest (August 9, 1942), Bihar crowds uprooted rail lines; rail services fully broke down; most affected area → Munger.

85-054.r: Jaya Prakash Narayan gained recognition as national leader in Quit India Movement; led underground work with Ram Manohar Lohia and Aruna Asaf Ali after leaders' arrest.

85-055.r: Jayaprakash Narayan escaped Hazaribagh jail with comrades on Deepawali (Diwali), November 9, 1942, during Quit India Movement.

85-057.r: Jai Prakash Narayan escaped from high-security Hazaribagh Jail during Quit India (1942) and organised underground activities.

85-058.r: Brothers Gangaram and Kheemdev martyred in police firing at Almora during Quit India Movement, 1942 (named Gangadutt and Kheemananda in Dictionary of Martyrs).

85-059.r: Not linked to Quit India → Shanti Ghosh. Quit India women: Matangini Hazra (73, shot at Tamluk, Bengal), Kanaklata Barua (Mrityu Bahini, Gohpur, Assam), Aruna Asaf Ali.

85-060.r: Quit India awakened and encouraged people because they absorbed Gandhi's 'Do or Die' slogan (August 8, 1942); A and R true, R explains A.

85-061.r: RSS stayed away from Quit India 1942 (A true); Reason (feared freedom would be delayed) false; RSS joined no national movement from 1940 to 1947.

85-062.r: Quit India brought British and Muslims closer: Jinnah's Muslim League condemned it, stayed with the British, said lawlessness would follow British exit; A and R true, R explains A.

85-063.r: Aruna Asaf Ali → major underground organiser of Quit India Movement; hoisted Congress flag at Gowalia Tank Ground (now August Kranti Ground), Bombay, 1942.

85-066.r: Quit India parallel governments → Ballia (August 1942, Chittu Pandey), Satara, Tamluk-Midnapore (Tamralipta Jatiya Sarkar, December 1942 to August 1944). Not Hazaribagh, Meerut, Agra.

85-071.r: Kanaklata Barua shot dead (Quit India, 1942) while hoisting national flag at police station of Gohpur subdivision, Sonitpur district, Assam.
85-071.t: Don't confuse: Gohpur is the place; Sonitpur is only its district.

85-072.r: Quit India marked culmination of national movement; it showed British rule was unwanted, so a mechanism for transfer of power was needed; A and R true, R explains A.

85-073.r: C. Rajagopalachari's pamphlet 'The Way Out' (1944) → solution to Congress-Muslim League constitutional deadlock; offered League Pakistan based on plebiscite.

85-074.r: 'Operation Rubicon' → British secret code word, to be used if Gandhi died during his fast unto death in Aga Khan Palace (Quit India period).

86-001.r: Subhas Chandra Bose: born 23 January 1897, Cuttack (Odisha); ICS 1920; Congress President 1938 and 1939; founded Forward Bloc 1939; fled to Germany 1941.

86-002.r: Forward Bloc → founded by Subhas Chandra Bose in 1939 after resigning Congress presidency (Tripuri crisis); title 'Netaji' first used in Germany.

86-007.r: Bose: escaped house arrest January 1941; formed Provisional Government of India, Singapore, October 21, 1943. Wrong: 1938 session was Haripura (51st), not Tripuri (52nd, 1939).
86-007.t: Don't confuse Haripura 1938 (Gujarat) with Tripuri 1939 (Madhya Pradesh); Bose presided both.

86-008.r: INA brainchild → Giani Pritam Singh Dhillon and Major Iwaichi Fujiwara (with Mohan Singh); INA formed under Mohan Singh's leadership.

86-010.r: Idea of Indian National Army, among options → Captain Mohan Singh (Giani Pritam Singh and Major Fujiwara not listed).

86-011.r: INA founded February 1942 under Mohan Singh, first commander; dissolved December 1942 after distrust over Japanese motives (clash with Rash Behari Bose's League).

86-012.r: First commander of Indian National Army → Mohan Singh.
86-012.t: Don't confuse: Mohan Singh first commander; Subhas Bose later Supreme Commander.

86-013.r: Azad Hind Sarkar (Provisional Government of Free India) declared 21 October 1943 in Singapore; Rash Behari Bose handed INA to Subhas Bose on 4th July 1943.

86-014.r: Provisional Government of Free India announced by Subhas Bose (INA Supreme Commander) on 21 October 1943; Singapore then part of British Malay.

86-015.r: Azad Hind Government (Arzi Hukumat-e Azad Hind, Singapore, October 1943) recognised by 9 countries: Japan, Germany, Italy, Thailand, Burma, Philippines, Manchukuo, Croatia... Indonesia did not.

86-017.r: Azad Hind Fauj set up October 1943 in Singapore (then part of British Malaya); Bose renamed Indian Independence League as INA.
86-017.t: Answer 'Malaya' if Singapore is absent from options, 'Singapore' if present.

86-019.r: Ras Bihari Bose helped Subhas Bose with Azad Hind Fauj; Subhas reached Tokyo June 1943, Rash Behari offered to resign as INA President; Subhas became Supreme Commander.

86-020.r: Not linked to Azad Hind Fauj → Major Kartar Singh. INA: Major General Shahnawaz Khan, Colonel Prem Kumar Sahgal, Colonel Shaukat Ali Malik.

86-021.r: Not linked to INA → S.A. Dange (Communist Movement). INA: Prem Singh Sehgal, Shah Nawaz Khan, General Mohan Singh.

86-022.r: Head office of Azad Hind Fauj (among options) → Rangoon (Yangon).

86-023.r: Not linked to INA → B.C. Dutta. Red Fort trials (November 1945): Sahgal, Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon, Shahnawaz → transportation for life; Abdul Rashid → 7 years.

86-024.r: 'Tum Mujhe Khoon Do, Main Tumhe Azadi Dunga' (Give me blood, I promise you freedom) → Subhash Chandra Bose, to soldiers in Burma.

86-025.r: Sheel Bhadra Yajee (Bihar) → joined Subhas Bose to found All India Forward Bloc; active in INA movement.

86-026.r: 'Free Indian Legion' → Subhas Bose in Germany (reached April 3, 1941; Free India Centre); about 10,000 prisoners from Rommel's North Africa battles, approved by Hitler.

86-027.r: Rani Jhansi (Laxmibai) Regiment → women's regiment of INA, formed 1943 by Subhas Chandra Bose.

86-029.r: 'Desh Nayak' → Rabindranath Tagore called Subhas Bose so (1938, Shantiniketan); Gandhi called him 'Patriot of Patriots'.
86-029.t: Don't swap: Desh Nayak = Tagore's title; Patriot of Patriots = Gandhi's title.

86-030.r: 'Chalo Delhi/Delhi Chalo' → Subhas Chandra Bose after taking INA command (earlier organised by Mohan Singh and Rash Behari Bose).

86-031.r: 'Jai Hind' → given by S.C. Bose; greeting of Azad Hind Fauj, now India's slogan.

86-032.r: Bose (Azad Hind Fauj) renamed Andaman → 'Shaheed' Island and Nicobar → 'Swaraj' Island.
86-032.h: Alphabet order: A before N, Sh before Sw → Andaman-Shaheed, Nicobar-Swaraj.

86-033.r: 'Azad Hind Fauj Day' → 12 November 1945; Azad Hind Fauj Week → 5 to 11 November 1945.

86-034.r: Rashid Ali (INA) → sentenced to seven years; Dhillon, Sahgal and Shahnawaz Khan tried at Red Fort, Delhi (1945) for waging war against the British.

86-035.r: Mohan Singh did not face Red Fort trials (November 1945); joint court-martial was of Prem Sahgal, Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon and Shahnawaz Khan.

86-036.r: INA Red Fort trials (November 1945): defence team headed by Bhulabhai Desai; included T.B. Sapru, Kailash Nath Katju, Jawaharlal Nehru.

86-038.r: INA Red Fort trial 1945 defence: Bhulabhai Desai, Tej Bahadur Sapru, K.N. Katju, J.L. Nehru, Asaf Ali. Not Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel.
86-038.h: Lawyers in court, Patel not: he never argued for INA.

86-043.r: Shah Nawaz Khan, Prem Kumar Sahgal, Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon → INA officers tried in Red Fort trial, 1945.

86-044.r: 1945 events: Wavell Plan (14 June), Shimla Conference (25 June-14 July), INA Trial (November). Naval Mutiny was 18-23 February 1946, not 1945.

86-045.r: Political Guru of Subhas Chandra Bose → C.R. Das.
86-045.t: Don't confuse with G.K. Gokhale, Gandhi's political guru.

86-046.r: CWC at Allahabad (April-May): Jawaharlal Nehru won majority for his plan of guerrilla war against the Japanese, given India's stand against Nazism, Fascism, imperialism.
86-046.c: Question dates this meeting to 1947, which does not fit a wartime plan against Japan; year looks misprinted.

87-001.r: Cabinet Mission led by Sir Pethick-Lawrence (Secretary of State for India); announced by PM Clement Attlee February 19, 1946; arrived Delhi 24 March 1946. Wavell not a member.

87-006.r: Three-tier polity → Cabinet Mission (arrived March 24, 1946): provinces in Groups A, B, C.

87-007.r: Cabinet Mission 1946 members: Pethick Lawrence (Secretary of State for India), Stafford Cripps, A.V. Alexander. Not members: Ramsay MacDonald, J. Andrew, Lord Emery.

87-010.r: Not in Cabinet Mission → John Simon (Simon Commission, report on Government of India Act 1919), William Wood. Members: Pethick Lawrence, Stafford Cripps, A.V. Alexander.

87-012.r: Cabinet Mission Plan (16 May 1946): still wanted united India → Union of British provinces and Princely states; rejected Muslim League's Pakistan demand.

87-014.r: Cabinet Mission 1946 → suggested reconstituting Viceroy's Executive Council with all portfolios, including War Member, held by Indian leaders.

87-015.r: Cabinet Mission (Delhi 24 March 1946; proposals 16th May 1946) recommended federal government: all India incl. Princely States; Centre → foreign affairs, defence, communication. Not courts or ICS.

87-017.r: Cabinet Mission (1946) sent to work out a constitutional arrangement for transfer of power; not to set up national government or work out Jinnah's Pakistan demand.

87-018.r: 1946: Muslim League withdrew acceptance of Cabinet Mission Plan (A true); League also joined interim government 1946 (R true), but R does not explain A.

87-019.r: Congress leader totally in favour of Cabinet Mission Plan → Mahatma Gandhi: 'best document the British Government could have produced in the circumstances'.

87-020.r: Congress President who negotiated with both Cripps Mission and Lord Wavell → Abul Kalam Azad (President 1940 to 1946).

87-021.r: Congress President during Cabinet Mission visit → Maulana Abul Kalam Azad; authorised by Working Committee, negotiated with Mission on 6 April 1946.

88-001.r: Constituent Assembly idea: first seen in 'Swaraj Bill' (1895); Swaraj Party demanded it at Ranchi (1934); officially stated by Congress at Faizpur session (1936).
88-001.t: Option 'Swaraj Party in 1935' has the wrong year; Swaraj Party's Ranchi demand was 1934.

88-002.r: Constituent Assembly that framed India's Constitution → set up under Cabinet Mission Plan; members from provincial legislative assemblies and chief commissioners' provinces.

88-004.r: Cabinet Mission: Constituent Assembly seats per province ≈ 1 per 10 lakh population, on communal basis; three voter classes: General, Muslims, Sikhs (Punjab only).

88-005.r: First session of Constituent Assembly → 9th December 1946; Rajendra Prasad elected permanent President on 11 December 1946.

88-006.r: Constituent Assembly President → Dr. Rajendra Prasad; Drafting Committee → B.R. Ambedkar; Union Power/Constitution Committees → Nehru; Fundamental Rights, Minorities advisory committee → Patel.
88-006.t: Don't confuse President of the Assembly (Rajendra Prasad) with Chairman of Drafting Committee (Ambedkar).

88-007.r: First President of Sovereign Constituent Assembly for Dominion of India → Rajendra Prasad; Assembly became sovereign on 15th August 1947.

88-008.r: Constituent Assembly elected by Provincial Assemblies in 1946 (Cabinet Mission): 296 British-province seats → Congress 208, League 73, independents 15; Jinnah not a member.

88-009.r: Socialist Party's National Executive (1946) demanded dissolving the Constituent Assembly and re-electing it by universal adult suffrage (Jayaprakash Narayan, Ram Manohar Lohia).

88-010.r: Sachchidananda Sinha → linked with Quit India Movement (per book); temporary Chairman at first meeting of Constituent Assembly, 9 December 1946.

88-011.r: G.V. Mavlankar → Speaker of Central Legislative Assembly (24 January 1946 to 14 Aug 1947) and of Lok Sabha (1952-1956); Bombay Assembly President 1937-1946.

89-001.r: Interim Government headed by Jawaharlal Nehru: announced 24th August 1946, took office 2nd September 1946; Muslim League did not join at first.

89-004.r: Interim (National Provisional) Government: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel → princely states portfolio, Home Affairs, Information and Broadcasting.

89-006.r: Interim Government 1946: Rajendra Prasad → Food and Agriculture; Baldev Singh → Defence; Jawaharlal Nehru → External Affairs and Commonwealth Relations.

89-007.r: Interim Cabinet 1946: Railways (Communication, Railways and Transport) → Asaf Ali.

89-008.r: Muslim League joined Interim Government October 1946; Liaquat Ali Khan → Finance Minister; his budget imposed high duties on traders and businessmen.

89-011.r: Interim Government 1946: Labour → Jagjivan Ram; Food and Agriculture → Rajendra Prasad; Law → Joginder Nath Mandal.

89-012.r: Interim Cabinet (2nd September 1946): Nehru, Patel, Rajendra Prasad, Rajagopalachari, Baldev Singh, Jagjivan Ram, Ali Zaheer; Liaqat joined later with League. Not members: B.R. Ambedkar, Abul Kalam Azad.

89-014.r: After 1946 elections Muslim League formed Government in Bengal; League leader and Prime Minister of the province → H.S. Suhrawardy.

89-015.r: Muslim League's 'Direct Action Day' → 16 August 1946; rejected Viceroy's interim cabinet plan, demanded separate Pakistan; riots followed.

90-001.r: At India's Independence, UK ruled by Labour Party; Prime Minister Clement Attlee (1945-1951).

90-003.r: Attlee declared in House of Commons on February 20, 1947 → British to leave India by June 1948; Mountbatten replaced Wavell, began power transfer March 1947.

90-004.r: Mountbatten came as Viceroy with instruction to keep India united if possible, after Attlee's 20th February 1947 announcement on transfer of power.

90-005.r: February 20, 1947: Attlee announced British withdrawal from India latest by 30 June 1948.

90-006.r: Mountbatten Plan → platform of Indian Independence; basis of transfer of power and partition; Mountbatten came March 1947, fixed 15 August 1947 for transfer.

90-008.r: Indian Independence Act, 1947 → partition into two dominions, India and Pakistan; Royal Assent 18 July 1947; dominions from 15 August 1947.

90-009.r: After Mountbatten Plan (June 3, 1947), British Parliament passed Indian Independence Act in July 1947; Royal Assent 18 July 1947; two dominions from 15 August 1947.
90-009.h: Plan June 3 → Assent July 18 → Freedom August 15.

90-012.r: Mountbatten Plan for partition officially declared June 3, 1947; formally approved by the British through the Indian Independence Act.

90-013.r: Britain freed India in 1947 because it had become weak in Second World War; A and R true, R explains A.

90-014.r: British sovereignty did not continue in free India (A false): no British control over dominions from 15 August 1947; but British sovereign appointed last Governor-General (R true).
